_meta.purpose: Representative positions for itinerary stops the expedition feed names but never places: the cruising days, passages and coastlines that ARE the voyage on an Antarctic or Arctic sailing.
_meta.appliedBy: scripts/place-named-waters.mjs (npm run place:waters), idempotent, re-run after every feed refresh
why: The Virtuoso feed gives every port its own coordinate and every day of open-water cruising none. That is honest for a port-to-port cruise and ruinous for an expedition: PONANT's Emblematic Antarctica is Ushuaia, two days of Drake Passage, five days of 'Antarctica (Cruising)', two more of Drake, Ushuaia. With only the two Ushuaia calls placed, the route is a place and itself, and the atlas has nothing to trace. 72 Antarctic sailings were in that state.

So these are NOT port corrections (port-overrides.json is for coordinates the feed got wrong). These are stops with no coordinate at all, given a representative one. It is written to the stop's fourth slot, never to its lat/lng, so every consumer that counts ports, filters by port or picks a gateway hotel keeps seeing exactly what the feed said. Only the route drawing reads it.

fields.key: short id written onto each stop it places; also the key of the shipped `waters` table
fields.names: the stop names exactly as the feed writes them
fields.label: what the map calls it
fields.radiusKm: 0 for a passage or a point; above 0 draws a soft zone, for an area whose landings are chosen on the day
fields.passage: true for water the ship passes THROUGH on the way somewhere (the Drake, the Inside Passage). Only passages are held to the detour test below; a place the ship goes TO (the peninsula, Shetland, a fjord) is the detour, so it only needs maxKm
fields.note: optional second line on the map label
fields.maxKm: the anchor is refused on a voyage none of whose real ports is this close: the same name can be a different sea on another ship
fields.water: an anchor that is open water sits on a sea cell of data/atlas/shared/landmask.bin, nudged a few km off the coast if needed, so build-sea-routes can sail to it. Fjords stay where they are: at 3.7 km cells they are walled off, and they are reached with the same short approach stub as a fjord port

placement: An anchor is only placed where it fits between the voyage's real ports. Each run of unplaced stops sits between two placed ones, A and B. If A and B are the same port (an out-and-back from Ushuaia) the run is a loop and is accepted. Otherwise a PASSAGE must lie roughly on the way: the path A -> passage -> B may be at most DETOUR times the direct distance, where A and B are the nearest fixed points either side (a real port, or a destination anchor). So a 'Northwest Passage' day between Erik Cove and Fury and Hecla Strait is left unplaced instead of bending the route a thousand kilometres west, while a Rio de Janeiro voyage that turns south for the Falklands and the peninsula keeps both.
Consecutive days at the same anchor collapse to one call on the map, labelled with the day range.

notPlaced.oceans: Indian Ocean, Atlantic Ocean, Caribbean Sea, Mediterranean Sea, Baltic Sea, North Sea, Red Sea, Ionian Sea, South/East China Sea, Java Sea, Arafura Sea, Arabian Sea, Gulf of Thailand, Gulf of Alaska, Greenland Sea, Beaufort Sea, Labrador Sea: too big for one point to mean anything; the route already crosses them.
notPlaced.lines: Equator, International Dateline, Arctic Circle, The Arctic Circle: a crossing anywhere along a line, not a place.
notPlaced.unspecific: Cruise starts, Cruise ends, Captain's Choice, Scenic Cruising, To Be Announced, Islands & Fjords, Newfoundland, St. Lawrence River.
notPlaced.inland: Mosfellsheiði, Laugarvatn: shore excursions, not where the ship goes.
notPlaced.unverified: Neptune's Fan Sea (Raja Ampat): no position we can stand behind yet.
